Space facilities follow the same base turn structure as all bases in Multiversal: •Each Base Turn = 1 week of narrative time. •Turns are used to resolve facility operations, project progress, staff actions, and random or triggered events. •Turns can be paused if action-time events (e.g., combat, sabotage, espionage) interrupt ongoing systems. During a base turn, players or managers may:

If life support goes offline: • • All organic beings must pass a Constitution save (DC 14) each hour or take 1d6 damage and suffer 1 level of exhaustion. • • GMs may roll for System Degradation Events if redundancy protocols are lacking. •

Hangars are often primary targets during station breaches or boarding scenarios. A well-defended hangar includes: •Automated Blast Doors: AC 16, HP 75. Can be sealed in 1 round as a reaction. •Drone Defense Grid: Deploys 1d4 defense drones when unauthorized access is detected. •Emergency Purge Protocol: Flushes the hangar (Dex save DC 15 to avoid being ejected into space). •Intruder Alarms: Alerts nearby facility staff or AI systems; triggers lockdowns.

During each base turn, any staffed science module may attempt one project, analysis, or prototype action. These usually take 1–3 turns depending on complexity. Research projects may yield: •Blueprints (for modules, tech, or weapons) •Enhanced system functions (e.g., better shielding) •Story clues or alien communications •Resource conversion methods •XP rewards or Knowledge Points (KP) •Chaos events if things go very wrong… 💡 Tip: Some research rolls have chaotic side effects—especially when tampering with time, gravity, or unknown energy signatures. GMs should feel encouraged to roll d20 for "unexpected results" on failed critical experiments. abilities, blueprints, or lore.

•Clones with incomplete memories may feel "unfinished". •Jump Clones may experience dissociation if switched too often. •Experimental Clones may suffer hallucinations or personality fragmentation.

•Is a clone considered alive? Some factions treat clones as disposable, while others consider them full individuals. •Are there cloning regulations? Many governments heavily regulate cloning due to identity fraud risks and potential abuses. •What happens if a clone rebels? A clone with free will may refuse to serve its original.

Computers in Multiversal can be customized and upgraded with expansion slots, allowing players to tailor their systems for specific tasks. Expansion items range from encryption tools and hacking modules to combat support and environmental adaptations. This section details how expansion slots work, lists available upgrades, and provides rules for installing and swapping components.
Explosive Rounds deal splash damage to targets around the impact point: Targets within a specified radius must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking partial damage on a successful save.

Weapons with Precision Aim allow users to take a careful aim for increased accuracy and damage: The user can spend an action to gain advantage on the next attack roll and may add a bonus to the damage roll. Precision Aim is especially effective for sniper rifles and other high-accuracy weapons.
•Timed: Detonates after a set duration. •Remote: Activated via a remote control. •Triggered: Activates when touched, approached, or set off by another condition.

•Area of Effect: Defined by the explosive's blast radius. •Damage Calculation: Targets make a Dexterity saving throw to take half damage unless otherwise noted. •Cover & Protection: Heavy cover may reduce or negate damage.

Preparation & Placement •Crafting or Acquiring: Requires appropriate skills and materials or can be purchased. •Setting Up: Placing an explosive typically requires an action. Stealthy placement may require a Dexterity (Stealth) check.
Grants +5 bonus to Perception checks when surveying large areas remotely

•Crafting Time: Usually 1 day per charge or enhancement level. •Materials: Requires special resources (e.g., Stormsteel, Feywood, Crystallized Mana). •Skill Check: Arcana or Crafting check (DC 15+) to complete the upgrade.
